messages.text:
1. allow pasting into a not-yet-started sessions's prompt (including image)

2. make the session-moving prompt "live" same way as not-yet-started

push when compelete

I’ll trace how unstarted sessions handle prompt input and paste, then apply the same live editing behavior to the session-moving prompt. I’ll validate both changes, commit them, and push the current branch.

I’m treating “live” as keeping the prompt editable while the session is moving, with its text and images carried through when the move finishes. I’m checking the existing startup draft path so both states can use the same behavior.
I’m waiting for the input-path investigation before implementing both changes. I’ll continue through validation, commit, and push.

The TUI already has an editable startup draft, but it explicitly rejects clipboard paste and hides that draft during a move. I’ll enable both through the existing draft path, preserving text, images, and queued prompts when the destination session is ready.

Image support needs more than enabling paste: the standby submission code currently keeps only text, so it would drop an attached image. I’m checking the existing structured prompt format so images survive queueing and the handoff to the live session.
The moving prompt change is underway. I’m resolving image ownership during startup so pasted images survive when the session becomes ready.

I found a timing bug that matters for the moving prompt: the startup queue can still send to the source worker during a move. I’ll make delivery wait for the destination, so a prompt typed during the move reaches the right worker.
The fix now includes safe queue delivery during moves and image preservation through startup. Implementation is in progress; validation, commit, and push are still pending.
I’m continuing the implementation and integration. The key checks are that pasted images survive startup and that prompts entered during a move wait for the destination worker.

The moving composer’s text editing and queue/recall test passes. Clipboard work also needs to travel with its original composer: rebuilding the draft when startup finishes would lose an image paste still in progress. The implementation will transfer that pending work with the composer.
The moving text-input regression passes. Clipboard preservation and destination-only delivery are still being implemented; I’ll review and validate the combined changes before committing and pushing.

I’m continuing with the two implementation pieces in parallel: preserving clipboard work across startup, and queueing prompts safely through a move. They’ll be reviewed together before the final test run and push.

The implementation now carries both the prompt content and a stable submission ID through the startup queue. That preserves images on delivery or refusal, and lets recall withdraw the specific queued message even when two messages have identical text.
The changes are taking shape, and focused tests are running. I’ll continue with integration review, full required validation, commit, and push.

I’m handling a move-failure edge case: if a move fails or is cancelled, prompts waiting for that destination should return to an editable draft. They should not silently run on the retained source worker.
Independent review is underway. I’m also closing the recall and refusal-recovery races before the final validation run, commit, and push.
Review found two split-pane issues: an unfocused moving prompt could be clipped or appear focused. I’m fixing those so rendering and input agree about which prompt owns focus.

Review also found that delayed worker replies could lose their owner when the composer moves, and that exhausted acknowledgement retries could make accepted work resendable. I’m fixing both before accepting the change.
The fixes are still in progress. Review found interruption and retry cases that need correction before I can validate, commit, and push the result.
I’m continuing with the review fixes. The remaining work is to settle delayed replies and queued-prompt recovery, then run the complete required checks and push the validated commit.
The remaining fixes are underway, and the final validation run is prepared. I’ll commit and push after those checks pass.

The validator is ready and waiting for the final source changes. It will run all six touched crate suites and workspace Clippy, including the existing isolated upgrade tests for the protocol and store changes.
I’m waiting for the implementation agents to finish the review fixes; final validation is queued next.

The backend is ready. Focused tests pass for image delivery, destination-only move delivery, failure recovery, and retries that retain uncertain submissions under their original IDs. I’m reviewing those fixes while the frontend finishes its handoff and split-pane checks.
The backend fixes and focused tests are complete. Frontend integration and final review remain before the full validation run and push.

The follow-up review found one remaining delivery boundary: a delayed request can arrive after a move is cancelled, and a historical failed move can wrongly block later startup prompts. I’m binding queued prompts to the lifecycle they were entered during to distinguish those cases.
The final move-origin fix is underway. It will keep delayed prompts tied to their cancelled move while allowing prompts from a later resume to queue normally. Validation and push remain pending.
I’m waiting for the final implementation fixes, then I’ll complete validation, commit, and push.

The move-origin regressions now pass: a delayed request after cancellation returns to its draft, and a historical failed move no longer blocks a later resume. I’m checking that the frontend preserves the same origin through paste, queueing, and handoff.

The delayed native-reply fix passed re-review. One small delivery guard still needs correction: prompts queued before a move must also wait for the destination worker when the session manager briefly exposes a stale source connection. I’m fixing that locally.
The stale-source guard is fixed, and focused tests are running for both ordinary and move-bound queued prompts. Frontend transport-retry checks are still finishing.

The shared delivery guard passed independent review. It now checks the destination worker for both ordinary startup prompts and prompts entered during a move, while allowing later resumes to ignore historical move failures.
Final backend validation is starting. The frontend’s focused handoff and rendering checks pass; its last transport-retry check is still finishing.

The full backend suites passed: core, client, and all 2,162 controller tests, including migration and move-delivery regressions. The remaining checks are the frontend suites and workspace Clippy once the final frontend fix is ready.

The frontend is ready, and its focused tests pass for image paste, handoff, split-pane rendering, recall, and retries after a failed connection. I’m starting the full frontend suites and Clippy, with one final review of saved-draft recovery during reconnect.

Upstream `master` has advanced during this work, including a protocol bump. After the current checks finish, I’ll merge those changes into this branch and validate the affected integration points before pushing.

The final recovery review confirmed two persistence bugs: reopening could append an already recovered image prompt twice, and a retry could lose part of its original request identity. I’m fixing both before delivery; they affect draft contents and whether work can be resent.
The recovery fixes are implemented, and targeted tests are next. Full validation and the upstream merge still need to finish before I push.

The frontend recovery regression passes: reopening preserves the original request, an accepted receipt clears its pending state, and an already recovered image appears only once. I’m completing the remaining checks before the upstream merge.
The targeted recovery regression passes. I’m waiting for the remaining validation results, then I’ll merge upstream and push the completed work.
Independent review accepted the recovery fixes. Final validation is still running; merge, commit, and push will follow.
All six touched crate suites, workspace Clippy, formatting, and diff checks passed. I’ll commit the validated changes now, merge upstream on the current branch, then check the integration and push.
Committed the implementation as `8f49f1413`. Upstream is merged with the combined protocol set to 66; final integration checks are running before I commit the merge and push.
Merge review passed. I’m waiting for the targeted integration checks, then I’ll commit the merge and push `master`.
